history.period: Saint's life 1279-1297; samadhi shrine ancient with later renovations (dates unverified)
history.summary: SHRINE-TYPE NUANCE: this is a samadhi shrine (memorial of a saint) managed by the Shri Sant Muktabai Sansthan, not a conventional deity temple - keep-or-drop decision needed. Sant Muktabai (Muktai, 1279-1297), younger sister of the first Varkari saint Dnyaneshwar, wrote about 41 abhangs, including the famous 'Tati ughada dnyaneshwara'; she is regarded as the first acknowledged female guru beyond the domestic realm in the Varkari tradition. Accounts of her death differ: some say she attained sanjivan samadhi, the prevailing belief being that she vanished in a flash of lightning at Mehun on the Tapi river. The ancient samadhi temple stands at Mehun village (Muktainagar taluka, ~15 km from Muktainagar); a newer temple complex has been built in Muktainagar town itself. The town, formerly Edlabad, is named Muktainagar after her.

name: Shri Sant Muktabai Sansthan (Muktabai Temple)
town_description: Muktainagar (formerly Edlabad) is a town in Jalgaon district on the banks of the Tapi river, about 35 km northeast of Jalgaon city. It is the taluka headquarters and is named after Sant Muktabai. CSV town corrected: 'Jalgaon' is the district; the Sansthan's temple is at Muktainagar (ancient samadhi shrine at Mehun village in the same taluka).
